name: USSF-627
destination_explanation: This orbit cleans up after itself. Dead satellites in the lowest orbits are pulled down by drag and burn up within a few years.
slot_a_text: A classified mission for the United States Space Force. It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites based on SpaceX’s Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches.
slot_b_text: B1103 is flying for the 7th time. It came down on the drone ship Of Course I Still Love You, 574 km downrange. Its previous trip was SDA Tranche 1 Transport Layer A, 32 days ago.

lg_slot_a_text: A classified mission for the United States Space Force. It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites based on SpaceX’s Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches.
lg_slot_b_text: That was B1103's 7th flight in 7 months. The mix: three Starlink, two SDA Tranche, one NROL, and one other. At its fastest it was back on the pad in 26 days.
lg_slot_c_text: That was SpaceX's 126th launch of the year, 745th all time. That is a launch every other day. No Falcon 9 has failed in 348 flights. It was the 263rd orbital launch attempt worldwide this year.
